title: a request whose client has gone is not run to its end, and not replayed after a restart
intention: When a request's asker has gone (its request() deadline passed, its socket closed, or it was handed over at a stop), the bus receipts the request given up and does not deliver it, live and after a restart; how a running handler is told is open-98ebd82e7a02.
why: Measured 2026-11-12: codemother ran a constrain ask under her shim lock for minutes after its asker's reach timed out at 120 s, starving every later codemother request; and a replaced bus took over unanswered asks whose envelopes still stood for delivery.
traces_to: The bus intention (outline 5.5.3.9: a wake never takes more than 60 s) and Law 1 (work nobody is waiting for spends the resolver on nothing).
how: Gate delivery on the asker: an envelope whose id is in the abandoned or handed-over set, or whose client socket closed, gets the given-up receipt instead of a handler. Running handlers per open-98ebd82e7a02. Red-first proof on a scratch bus counts a slow fixture handler's runs.

clauses.claim: an envelope whose asker's request() reached its deadline before delivery is receipted given up and its handler never runs
after a restart, an envelope the previous bus handed over as an ask is receipted given up by the next bus and its handler never runs
a request whose client socket closes before delivery is receipted given up and its handler never runs

decisions.text: D1: delivery in bus.py checks the envelope's id against _abandoned and the handed-over asks and writes the given-up receipt instead of calling the handler.
D2: server.py marks a call's request id abandoned when its client connection closes before the reply; the taking-over of handed-over asks at start feeds the same set.
D3: the red-first proof, one tooth per clause, on a scratch bus with a slow fixture device.

out: cairn/devices/codemother (a cooperative cancel there, if open-98ebd82e7a02 asks for one, is its own ticket)

orient.intent: The bus refuses before delivery any request whose asker has gone (deadline reached, client socket closed, or handed over at a stop), receipting it bus-asker-gave-up; a handler already running is not cancelled.

Law 7: the record of truth says why nobody took it (bus-asker-gave-up receipt)
